In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of SBRT for prostate treatment is safe and efficacious, with the caveat that the results are not yet long enough to make definitive statements regarding the impact of SBRT on long term toxicity, and that the results are still limited in the setting of high-risk patients.

there is no evidence to support a difference in outcomes between proton and photon based SBRT for the treatment of low and intermediate risk prostate cancer, and that the evidence does support a difference in cost.
proton-based SBRT for prostate carcinoma is not superior to photon-based SBRT in terms of tumor control and toxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the importance of accounting for the treatment delivery process when comparing photon and proton-based SBRT for prostate.
we have developed a new method for robustness and deliverability analysis that can be applied to any treatment site and any treatment delivery method (e.g. IMRT, SBRT, SRS).
the photon-based SBRT plan has the best dosimetric quality, the proton-based plan is the most robust and has the best treatment efficiency, while the hybrid plan is a compromise between the two.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, the proton treatment plans for SBRT prostate treatment are more robust than photon treatment plans.
, for the prostate, the dose distribution is not the only factor that matters when comparing proton and photon-based SBRT.
